chunks: My father, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, who ascribed it (to the Imam), saying: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at a man who had come out of the bath with his hands dyed (with henna). Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: Does it please you that Allah, Exalted and Glorious, had created your hands like this? He said: No, by Allah. I only did that because it reached me from you that: 'The one who enters the bath, let the effect of it be visible on him,' meaning henna. So he said: It is not as you think. The meaning of that is: when one of you comes out of the bath and is safe (from impurity), let him pray two rak'as out of thankfulness.
ai.seo_question: What is the correct meaning of 'let the effect of the bath be visible' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar* illustrates the Shia scholarly distinction between cultural customs (*'urf*) and religious injunctions (*shari'ah*), clarifying that the Prophet's and Imams' recommendation to show the effects of bathing was often misinterpreted as a requirement for henna. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) redirects this practice toward spiritual gratitude (*shukr*), linking physical purification with the ritual prayer of thanksgiving, thereby emphasizing the inner dimension of worship over mere external appearance.
